Subject: Multi-year pricing: anchored rate + renewal reset ask

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with latency and the per-route observability. We're preparing our procurement recommendation and have an ask around commercial structure before we take this to our CFO.

High level: Aeromed is comfortable with a 3-year commitment but needs a firm "anchored" starting price and a predictable renewal/reset mechanism that prevents unbounded uplift at renewal. Specific requests:
- 3-year term, $1.8M ARR committed in year 1 (ramped consumption in years 2-3).
- Price locked for first 12 months (no uplift).
- A capped annual uplift formula for years 2 and 3 (not to exceed 8% per year).
- Renewal protection: if Redwood's published list price increases >10% year-over-year, Aeromed requests the ability to exit at renewal or trigger an escrow/true-up instead of a full pass-through.

I've attached our redline (Aeromed_RFP_Q3_redline.pdf) and a simple model (AER-7421-MAP.xlsx). Can you let me know whether Redwood can sign to a structure like this or if we need an exec exception?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement hopes to finalize vendor shortlist by EOW.

Best,

Irene — quick calcs below.

Baseline: Aeromed's proposed $1.8M ARR first-year commit vs list would be ~28% discount across their expected SKU mix. Under standard deal desk policy we can approve up to 20% off list for this segment; anything beyond needs exec signoff.

Options to propose to Aeromed (sorted by cost to Redwood):
1) Standard compromise (recommended): 3-year term, 12-month hard lock, uplift cap 6%/yr (yrs 2–3), with an escrow-style true-up if our list increases >12% year-over-year. Require minimum monthly committed spend floor and quarterly usage reporting. Expected revenue delta vs their ask: ~ +$120k ARR vs their 8% cap scenario.
2) Executive concession: accept 8% cap yrs 2–3 and renewal opt-out only if published list >15% (higher threshold). Requires VP signoff and 1.5% price-add to initial effective price to offset risk.
3) Protective structure (lower risk): 3-year term, 12-month lock, then flexible uplift tied to regional CPI + 3% but with a hard cap of 7%. Also include automatic fallback to a higher-performance model if unit economics degrade. Operationally heavier.

Attachments: quick impact workbook in-line (see AER-7421-MAP.xlsx).

Ask: Vivek — can you approve option 1 (recommended) or option 2 (exec concession)? If option 2 we need to route a clean sign-off and legal redline on the renewal protection.

-Jordan

Thanks for the analysis. I reviewed the numbers and Aeromed looks like a strategically relevant account in healthcare — granting some protection makes sense so long as we mitigate rollback risk. I approve moving forward with Jordan's Option 1 with the following mandatory conditions:

Required conditions (must be in contract):
- 3-year term; year 1 price hard-locked (no uplift).
- Uplift cap: 6% per year for years 2 and 3 (absolute cap).
- If Redwood's published list price increases >12% year-over-year, rather than immediate pass-through, we will:
  a) place the incremental delta into an escrow account for that renewal period;
  b) Aeromed may either accept the escrow payment distribution or terminate at renewal with a 60-day notice.
- Minimum monthly committed spend floor of $120,000 in year 1 (to prevent heavy ramp-downs).
- Quarterly usage reports and a 30-day remediation window for abnormal consumption patterns.

Operational asks before signature:
- Legal to redline the attached draft-SLA-reset-clause.docx with the escrow language and termination mechanics.
- Deal desk to prepare a short internal fallback plan if Aeromed exercises termination at renewal (repurchase credits, transfer assistance).

I want the external response to be crisp and to highlight the safeguards — offer the 6% cap + escrow as our preferred path; escalate option 2 only if they push back.

Vivek Kulkarni
